tes femmes de bien, & honeſtes, le recog
noiſtront: & que ce pendant ladite de
Rols, ores eſtant en la puiſſance. dudit
Pierre Guerre, demeurant en ſa maiſon,
fuſt ſequeſtrée, & miſe en quelque mai-
ſon de gens de bien, ou ne peuſt eſtre ſe-
duite, ni ſubornée. Au reſte, concluant
Si par les vulgaires & communes reigles de droict, il
eſt à grande raiſon defendu ſequeſtrer les biens {a}: c'eſt
à dire les ſeparer de la main & puiſſance du poſſeſſeur,
pour les mettre és mains tierces {b}. parce qu'on ne doit
pas facilement, ni ſans vrgentes raiſon, & cognoiſſance
de cauſe priuer aucun de la poſſeſſion de ſon bien {c}.
A plus forte raiſon, la ſequeſtration & ſeparation des
perſonnes doit eſtre prohibee: meſmement, quand ou
les veult oſter de la compagnie de ceux qui luy appar-
tiennent de bien pres: comme ſont peres, & meres
enfans ou autre prochains parẽs {d}. Et au contraire auſſi,
tout ainſi que quand il y a bonne & ſuffiſante cauſe,
(comme eſt vne crainte que les parties ne viennent
aux armes {e}, & ſoupçon de fuite, ou de poureté {f}.) il eſt
indubitalement permis ſequeſter le bien meuble, &
les fruis de l'immeuble {g}: pareillement aux perſonnes,
ne fault faire difficulté, que quand il y a quelque ſoup
çon, & crainte de ſeduction, ou autre cauſe legitime,
le Iuge ne puiſſe iuſtement proceder à la ſequeſtration
d'vn homme, ou d'vne femme: & la mettre en la cõpa-
gnie de gens de bien, qui la gardent de parler, & con-
uerſer auec perſonnes ſuſpects {h}. Comme par
exemple', ſi le mari demande eſtre reintegré de ſa
femme, laquelle toutesfois iuſtement craint ſon au

uncertain.note: a thin slanted comma-shaped mark stands at cap height immediately left of 'accarez', on the column's left edge, clear of the letter (pages/strips/p037/body-2.jpg, top left). It is much lighter than the apostrophes of 'ſ'aſſeurant' and 'qu'elles' on the same line and than the raised sort after 'exemple' (blocks[3].lines[22]), so it may be a stray sort or offset ink rather than type; kept as printed as an apostrophe. Line ends 'tou' with no hyphen (continues 'tes')

uncertain.note: a small raised comma-shaped sort, clearly inked, stands between 'exemple' and the comma at ascender height (pages/strips/p037/body-8.jpg, line 3, at 6x). Transcribed as an apostrophe; its purpose is unclear, probably a stray sort

uncertain.text: Et que ſes femme, & ſeurs, luy fuſſent
uncertain.note: sic: 'ſes femme' (plural determiner, singular noun); 'fuſſent' is ſſ

uncertain.text: Rols, ores eſtant en la puiſſance. dudit
uncertain.note: the mark after 'puiſſance' is a compact round dot on the baseline with no descending tail (both readers, 8x-9x), so a period, not a comma; sic mid-sentence
at 6x the mark after XX is a wedge with a tail descending below the baseline, unlike the round dot after ANNOTAT: a comma, sic for the usual period

uncertain.text: enfans ou autre prochains parẽs {d}. Et au contraire auſſi,
uncertain.note: 'parẽs': the mark over the e is a thick nearly horizontal wavy bar (tilde), not the thin slanted acute of 'reintegré' on line 22; easy to misread as 'parés'

uncertain.text: d'vn homme, ou d'vne femme: & la mettre en la cõpa-
uncertain.note: the line-end break sign after 'cõpa' is a short raised blob rather than a clean dash; transcribed '-'

uncertain.text: femme, laquelle toutesfois iuſtement craint ſon au
uncertain.note: the page ends mid-word: 'au' has no hyphen and continues on p038; no catchword is printed

the last sort is a p with an abbreviation stroke: at 10x (pages/strips/p037/margin-2.jpg, note a line 1) the stroke curls off the descender to the right as a flourish rather than a straight bar crossing it, i.e. ꝓ (pro); the continuation 'hib.' (= prohib.) confirms pro. A ꝑ with a blotted bar cannot be wholly excluded
first letter read as h, not b (open arch at bottom right, unlike the closed bowl of the b two glyphs later); citation resolves to C. de prohibita sequestratione pecuniae

at 8x (pages/strips/p037/margin-2.jpg, note c line 1) the letter after v has a short ascender with a hooked crossbar and a curved foot, the same sort as the t of the agreed 'vtr.' in note d: 'vt'. An italic e is the alternative. The last word is an over-inked blob read 'lis' (vt lis pend. = ut lite pendente); its last letter could be 'a'
'l' carries no period here (contrast 'l.licet' in note b); transcribed as printed
'confi' with an fi ligature (clear crossbar, so f not ſ; continues 'tetur'); line ends without a hyphen
the points in this citation line are faint; the isolated tall sort after 'app.' carries no dot and is read as l (could be a b with a thin bowl); the mark after 'app' may be a colon
'ijs' is printed with the italic fount's ij sort (two dots over the pair); transcribed 'ijs' per house practice. No period is printed after the P

at 4x (pages/strips/p037/margin-4.jpg, note h line 2) a slanted grave stroke sits directly over the o of 'ro', at accent height and clear of the line above (the 'l.' above it has no descender): read as a printed grave, 'ſi ve-rò' = si vero. Reader B took it for a stray mark

the word before the line end is an over-inked blot about two sorts wide, read 'ex' since the next line is 'hib.' (D. de liberis exhibendis); at 8x there is only a very faint grey smear to its right, far lighter than the printed hyphens of this margin, so no hyphen is transcribed (a break without a hyphen is normal in this print). The blot could also be read 'exe' or 'œ'
